LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mean_codebookOutp: Let q be a law on words over a finite input alphabet. Draw M ≥ 1 codewords independently from q, choose a message uniformly and independently of the codebook, and send its codeword through the block channel K. Averaged over the codebook, message and channel output, the error probability of the decoder for A is at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A). Here J is the joint law of a word drawn from q and its output under K, and S is the product of their marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_mem_suppor: For M ≥ 1, some codebook in the support of M independent draws from q has average error through K, using the decoder for event A, at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A). Here J is the input–output joint law and S the product of its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_blockChann: Let q be a law on length-n input words for a finite memoryless channel. Write J for the joint law of an input word drawn from q and its output, and S for the product of their marginals. For any acceptance event A and M ≥ 1, some codebook in the support of M independent draws from q has average error at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A) with the decoder for A.

Let J be the joint law of an input word drawn from q and its output through Wⁿ, and S the independent product of its marginals. For any real t and M ≥ 1, some codebook in the support of M iid draws from q, using the decoder for A = {z : J(z) > exp(t)S(z)}, has average error at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)exp(−t).
